notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Arizona county candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Arizona yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: Navajo County Sheriff's Office has been using automatic license plate readers since 2013.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS000033, citing The Tribune

redFlags.label: Private camera registry
redFlags.detail: The Navajo County Sheriff's Office maintains a voluntary registry of private and personal surveillance cameras through Motorola Solutions' CityProtect platform.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS002552, citing CityProtect

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Navajo County Sheriff's Office operates one DJI Phantom drone as of 2017, according to data compiled by the Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS003612, citing Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 13 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Show Low's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
